newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end listless session lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end listless session lower.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2364 -4 US 30yr cl 6.86 +0.05
*Stocks ended weaker in listless trade with the market unmoved by Q3 inflation data. Turnover 334.1 million shares, A$645.4 million value, 1,064 stocks traded, 324 steady, 403 rises, 337 falls
Australian shares closed slightly weaker in listless trade on Wednesday, the market unmoved by the release of third quarter inflation data and weighed down by a Dow pullback on Tuesday.
Key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 6.9 points lower at 2,346.7, off its intra-day low of 2,340.8.
The December share price index finished four points down at 2,364 and at an 17.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the 0.3 percent rise in the third quarter CPI was well within market expectations. As a result, investors were still unsure about the timing of a possible monetary easing.
"This has been the quietest session we have had for a while," a Sydney-based dealer said. "I think the market decided to take a breather after some pretty busy trading in the past week and a half."
The dealer said third quarter inflation data took away some of the enthusiasm for the bank sector seen earlier and generally put the brakes on a mid-morning market recovery.
"At one stage the resource sector looked like getting some support but after the CPI data I think investors decided to wait and see what Wall Street does tonight," the dealer said.

Westpac stock remained in the limelight following recent speculation that National Australia Bank could be a potential bidder for the bank if Australian bank ownership rules are relaxed by the federal government.
The bank's shares continued to rise even though National Australia Bank was now not considered to be the buyer of a A$130 million parcel of converting preference shares on Monday.

The shares of food and beverage company Coca-Cola Amatil continued their steep slide. Dealers said the market was still in the process of reweighting the company after a Sydney broker put a sell recommendation on the stock last week.

In other markets, Australian bonds pulled back from their stronger opening levels after third quarter inflation data was well within market expectations. The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.53 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's closing levels. The Australian dollar continued to hover just above the US$0.7940 support level after the market gave a muted reponse to the inflation data.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade remained at moderate levels as activity slowed in line with the physical market.
